doc.title: David Finck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, May 29, 2015

title: Milt Hinton, George Duvivier and Jerry Bruno
summary: Finck tells his one Milt Hinton story and speaks of George Duvivier and Jerry Bruno.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: [audio interlude “Old Man Time” by Milt Hinton]
Do you have a Milt Hinton story?

I only have one Milt Hinton story, because I didn’t really know him. But one day I was entering the musicians union and I had my bass and I had an amplifier I think, at the same time. And it was like one of those days in New York where it was like 200 degrees and humid. And I went through the door of the union and I hit the cold air and I was like ahhh man. It just felt great to have the air conditioning finally descend upon me. And I hear this guy say, “hey man, what’s the matter with you?” He said, “when I came up there

wasn’t any air conditioning in this building.” And I looked up and it was Milt. He had the hat and everything else. I go, “are you Milt Hinton?” “That’s right.” He was nice. I chatted with him very briefly. But I did know he’s clearly a great bass player. There are a lot of great stories about him. And the other guy from that era who is unbelievable is George Duvivier. George played on zillions of records. I knew him a little bit. I subbed for him a couple of times back in you know, 1982. And there’s another bass player that a lot of people don’t know about named Jerry Bruno. Jerry is 90 something, maybe 95 years old. When I tell you this guy knows everything. He knows everything. Every song. He’s unstumpable. Every alternate chord. A wonderful musician.
Is he a New Jersey person?
Yeah, a lot of good musicians. Bucky [Pizzarelli].
Bucky’s there. He and Bucky go back forever. Yeah.
